Mozambique was implementing institutional capacity-building reforms as part of its broader 2004/05 public financial management reform agenda. The main medium- to long-term capacity-building measures identified were: (i) strengthening sectoral and central-level capacities for policy analysis, sector strategy planning, expenditure policy development, and medium-term planning and budgeting; and (ii) strengthening the capability of the Repartições de Finanças to prepare tax assessments and undertake tax collection more efficiently.

Implementation status: Ongoing/planned during the 2004/05 assessment period, with reforms framed as medium- to long-term institutional strengthening measures. In parallel, an ongoing civil service reform programme continued to be implemented.

Timelines: The civil service reform was described as a key element of the 2000–2004 five-year plan and as continuing at the time of the assessment. For PFM reform management, a review/management workshop was strongly recommended for early February 2006, and some related PFM actions were targeted for the 1st quarter of 2006.

Milestones achieved: Institutional capacity needs had been identified and formally incorporated into the reform agenda; reform measures were categorized in the PFM assessment, and existing PFM reform coordination arrangements were already in place, though needing strengthening.

Milestones to achieve: Build stronger analytical and planning capacity at sectoral and central levels; improve medium-term budgeting capacity; enhance tax administration skills and efficiency at Repartições de Finanças; and strengthen coordination of reform actions across government.

Responsible agencies: Ministries of Finance and Planning were central to the reform effort. Other entities mentioned in reform coordination included Tribunal Administrativo, UTRAFE and UTRESP. The Repartições de Finanças were specifically relevant for tax administration capacity building.

Donor partners: The civil service reform was noted as continuing with World Bank support. The report was prepared for the Government of Mozambique and Programme Aid Partners (PAPS), indicating broader donor engagement in the reform dialogue.

The evidence is descriptive of actual reform programs and plans in Mozambique during the 2004/05–2006 period, not merely legal rules.
